question: What is the approximate total refracting power of the human eye, and which structure contributes the greatest share?

answers.text: 60 D total; the lens contributes approximately 43 D

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The lens contributes only about 16–20 D, not 43 D. The cornea is the dominant refracting structure.

answers.text: 60 D total; the cornea contributes approximately 43 D

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The eye has ~60 D total power; the cornea accounts for ~43 D and the lens ~16–20 D. This distinction is fundamental to understanding corneal refractive surgery.

answers.text: 40 D total; the cornea and lens contribute equally

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The total power is ~60 D, not 40 D, and the contributions are not equal — the cornea dominates.

answers.text: 80 D total; the vitreous contributes approximately 20 D

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The vitreous is not a refracting element. Total power is ~60 D, predominantly from the cornea.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the optics of the eye section. The cornea provides the majority (~43 D) of the ~60 D total refracting power.
Well recalled. The cornea provides ~43 D (~72%) of total refracting power — that is why corneal curvature changes in LASIK produce large refractive corrections.
